result:
I've built the `incident` bed in `beds/incident/`, and all 13 tests pass with `node --test beds/incident/` (about 15 s). No model has been run on it yet, so the claim that cheap single-shot models usually fail from difficulty 3 is a design target, not a measurement.

**Files** (all in `/home/user/workflow-foundry/beds/incident/`):
- `index.mjs`: the contract interface, including the output schema, its validator, the oracle with the exact pass rule, `referenceSolve` and 7 bad controls.
- `gen.mjs`: generator and per-difficulty knobs. It builds the topology, propagates the fault along hard caller edges with delays, handles fallback-only callers and red herrings, renders 5 log styles, and writes the service map and the ticket.
- `catalog.mjs`: reworked from the partial file the earlier agent left. It has 9 fault classes with paraphrase pools sampled per task, plus all the red-herring and injection vocabulary.
- `baseline.mjs`: three script baselines (first sustained error jump, most ERROR lines, keyword grep) that read only the task inputs.
- `incident.test.mjs`: the 13 tests.
- `index.js`: shim so `node --test beds/incident/` resolves, the same pattern as gridquest and kinetics.
- `README.md`: everything the brief asked for, plus measured script-baseline rates and known limits.

**Tests (13):**
- Interface and schema portability.
- Determinism, task shape, and files matching inputs.
- `referenceSolve` passes on 200 tasks: 20 seeds × 5 difficulties × 2 splits.
- All 7 bad controls fail on 20 seeds per difficulty: `empty`, `shuffled-or-corrupted`, `plausible-but-wrong` (blames the first-hop caller), `sibling-class`, `late-timestamp`, `impacted-missing-half`, `follow-red-herring`.
- Schema-invalid output is rejected; the ±60 s boundary and the Jaccard 0.8 boundary are checked.
- No truth leakage: the true class id never appears in the data, class ids appear in the log only inside injected lines, no misleading claim matches the truth, and ticket times are always more than 60 s after the fault start.
- Structural invariants hold, and every dependent failure line names an affected service through an alias the service map documents.
- The root is the top ERROR emitter in at most 20% of seeds (measured: 1 of 300).
- The script baselines pass at most 25% of seeds at difficulty 3 and above.
- At difficulty 5, generate and oracle each take under 2 s and grow memory by under 200 MB, measured in a fresh process.

**Token sizes** (prompt + inputs via `estimateTokens`, dev seeds 0–59, min / median / max):

| Difficulty | Services | Lines (median) | Tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6 | 327 | 8,204 / 9,144 / 9,974 |
| 2 | 8 | 424 | 10,908 / 12,331 / 13,258 |
| 3 | 11 | 472 | 12,841 / 14,432 / 16,985 |
| 4 | 14 | 1,751 | 44,592 / 49,072 / 55,678 |
| 5 | 18 | 4,250 | 100,293 / 114,709 / 128,910 |

**Script baselines** (passes out of 60 seeds; the most-ERROR-lines script passed 0 at every level):

| Difficulty | First error jump | Keyword grep |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 17 | 21 |
| 2 | 25 | 17 |
| 3 | 4 | 1 |
| 4 | 2 | 0 |
| 5 | 0 | 0 |

**Anything incomplete:**
- The fault class is drawn uniformly per seed, not stratified: over 300 seeds the per-class counts ranged from 21 (`upstream_rate_limiting`) to 41.
- Difficulty 5 is about 115K tokens, as the brief asked (~4,000 lines). That is large for the local 2B/4B models.
- `catalog.mjs` shows as modified in git because the earlier agent's version was already tracked. Nothing is committed.
- Python wasn't needed, so there is no sandbox helper.

The `records` bed is finished: all 12 tests pass with `node --test beds/records/` (about 18 s).

**Tests**
- `referenceSolve` scores 1.0 on 20 dev seeds at each difficulty, plus a few test-split seeds.
- Every bad control fails on all 20 seeds at every difficulty, and on 60 per difficulty in development runs. The controls are `empty`, `shuffled-or-corrupted`, `no-dedup`, `ignore-void-markers`, `oldest-row-wins`, `us-locale-dates` and `unconverted-amounts`.
- A separate solver that reads only `task.inputs` scores 1.0 on every task (100 in the suite, 250 across both splits in development). This shows the answer can be derived from the text alone.
- The suite also covers determinism, schema rejection, oracle tolerance, no-truth-leak checks, difficulty sanity and runtime. `generate` and `oracle` take about 10–50 ms at d5.

**Input size per difficulty** (estimated tokens of prompt + inputs, 30 dev seeds):

| | rows | tokens, average [range] | real people, average [range] |
|---|---|---|---|
| d1 | 30 | 3,403 [3,350..3,475] | 16 [13..19] |
| d2 | 55 | 4,768 [4,604..4,955] | 28 [23..34] |
| d3 | 85 | 6,445 [6,248..6,625] | 41 [35..51] |
| d4 | 115 | 7,656 [7,380..7,883] | 55 [46..61] |
| d5 | 150 | 9,036 [8,821..9,381] | 68 [59..76] |

**Pass rule:** pass when field accuracy over matched people is at least 0.97, pairwise cluster F1 is at least 0.95, and extra and missing people are each at most floor(0.02·E), where E is the number of real people. Below 50 people that allows none, which covers d1–d3. Score = harmonic mean(field accuracy over all people, pair F1) × (1 − (extra + missing)/E).

**Things that differ from the brief:**
- **Extra output field.** The output includes `source_rows` (all row ids merged into a person). The cluster F1 needs it; `entity_id` alone doesn't say which rows belong together.
- **`package.json` shim.** On Node 24.21, `node --test beds/records/` does not expand a directory; it tries to load it as a module and fails. The small `package.json` in my directory points `main` at the test file so that exact command works. Other bed families will hit the same problem.

**Incomplete:**
- No model has been run on this bed. The claim that a cheap single-shot model usually fails at d≥3 is a design expectation, backed only by the ablation table in the README (removing one skill from the text-level solver).
- Not every skill is decisive on its own. Ten are at d5 (each fails at least 12 of 20 tasks when knocked out). Nicknames, accent restoration, era dates and the 011 prefix each cost only a few fields per task.
- The VENDEX free text uses three sentence templates, so it is semi-structured rather than open-ended prose.
- The text solver shares the rule code with the oracle. It proves the text carries the answer, but not that the code matches the prose spec; I checked that by hand.

No commits made. `pools.mjs` and `render.mjs` were kept from the interrupted agent and edited; they had already been committed by someone else in a "WIP snapshot" (2a4bde3), so `render.mjs` now shows as modified in git. No Python sandbox was needed.

Files are in /home/user/workflow-foundry/beds/records/:
- `index.mjs`
- `world.mjs`
- `render.mjs`
- `pools.mjs`
- `solve-text.mjs`
- `records.test.mjs`
- `measure.mjs` (reproduces the README tables: `node beds/records/measure.mjs 30`)
- `README.md`
- `package.json`
